clue.text: Appointment tip — finally managed call after dinner

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word just before it

blocks.note: a post is a job or appointment
the closing letter of tip
ran a business means managed it
to dial a number is to call it

explanation.surface: Someone books an appointment, leaves a tip, and finally gets round to a phone call once dinner is over.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective comes from Latin prandium, a meal, and describes things happening following a main meal, like a speech or stroll.

clue.text: Unusually plain about introduction of organ, a musical instrument

indicators.note: something done unusually is not done in the normal order, so the letters get rearranged
an introduction is the start, so only the opening letter of the next word is used
about means around, so the rearranged letters wrap round the single letter

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
the opening letter of organ
taken as written

explanation.surface: An oddly simple organ piece is introduced as part of a musical performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A pianola is a player piano, a keyboard instrument that plays itself from perforated paper rolls.

clue.text: Service’s opening recollected litany, holy

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter alone
read as re-collected, gathered up again in a different order

blocks.note: the first letter of service
these six letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A worshipper recalls the litany that opened a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recollected' looks like plain remembering in the surface; split as re-collected it signals a reshuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are adjectives describing deep goodness and religious devotion, so they act as near synonyms.

clue.text: Careful before buying new pin? Yes, awfully

indicators.note: done awfully means done badly, so the letters come out in a mangled order

blocks.note: these nine letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A shopper hesitates over whether to buy a new pin and agrees reluctantly.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is from the proverb 'penny-wise and pound-foolish': thrifty in small matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone thrifty over small sums takes pains with money, weighing up even trivial purchases before spending.

clue.text: Periodic inspection of car over time

blocks.note: a German make of car
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A car is checked over regularly, as at a service.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means the first piece sits above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: An audit is an official examination of accounts or procedures, typically carried out at regular yearly intervals.

clue.text: Become aware of record, not half modern

indicators.note: not half means one half of the word is dropped, keeping only the other

blocks.note: a disc is a gramophone record
the front half of this word will be dropped

explanation.surface: Someone notices a record that is only partly up to date.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the first three of six letters leaves the back half.
explanation.definitionFit: To discern is to perceive or detect something, often with effort, so it means coming to notice it.

clue.text: A non-drinker, Bill, he’s diplomat

blocks.note: taken as written
TT stands for teetotal, someone who drinks no alcohol
a bill is an account, abbreviated AC
taken as written

explanation.surface: A teetotal man called Bill turns out to work for the foreign service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name but is the account; the apostrophe s stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An attaché is a junior official posted to an embassy, a member of a country's diplomatic staff abroad.

clue.text: Regard as up to it and worthy of respect

blocks.note: to consider someone clever is to regard them as clever
someone up to a task is able to do it

explanation.surface: A candidate is judged competent and deserving of esteem.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides meaning large, the word has an older sense of notable or important, a person deserving regard.

clue.text: Too vain about good reception

indicators.note: about can mean turned around, so the letters are moved into a new order

blocks.note: these seven letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A conceited performer laps up the applause.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovation is sustained applause from an audience, the warm welcome given to a well-liked performance.

clue.text: Working area of the French king, the best

blocks.note: des is French for 'of the' with a plural noun
K is the chess abbreviation for king
the top is the best of anything

explanation.surface: Somewhere the French king works in his finest surroundings.
explanation.definitionFit: A desktop is the flat surface of a desk, or a computer's home screen, both places where tasks are done.

clue.text: Friend about to interfere slyly, securing advantage

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word's letters go round the rest
something done slyly is done deviously, so the letters are slipped into a disguised order

blocks.note: a pal is a friend
these nine letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A friend is about to meddle cunningly to gain the upper hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Friend' looks like part of the anagram but is a separate three-letter word that wraps round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Preferential treatment gives someone priority or favour over others, so it confers an edge on them.

clue.text: In impatient way before long

blocks.note: first meaning: curtly, brusquely
second meaning: soon

explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means both speaking abruptly and with irritation, and happening in a little while from now.

clue.text: Syrup strangely clear — note covers it

indicators.note: strangely means in an odd way, so the letters appear in an odd order
to cover something is to wrap round it, so the note goes on either side

blocks.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
these five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd observation that a syrup looks unexpectedly clear.
explanation.definitionFit: Treacle is the thick dark sugar syrup left from refining, sold in Britain as golden syrup or molasses.

clue.text: Record help going west by railway

indicators.note: in an across clue, heading west means reading right to left

blocks.note: aid is help
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: Someone notes down that help is arriving by train from the east.
explanation.definitionFit: A diary is a daily written log of events and appointments, a personal journal kept over time.

clue.text: Fury about knight because false

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for anger wraps round the rest

blocks.note: ire is anger
N is the chess notation for knight
since can mean because

explanation.surface: Someone is enraged by a knight who has been disloyal.
explanation.definitionFit: Insincere describes someone not genuinely meaning what they say, so their words are hypocritical or untrue.

clue.text: Certain about cleaner ultimately deserving extra payment

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for sure is wrapped round the next pieces
ultimately means at the very end, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: sure means certain
a char, or charwoman, is a British word for a cleaner
the final letter of deserving

explanation.surface: Someone is sure the cleaner merits a bonus.
explanation.definitionFit: A surcharge is an additional fee added on top of the usual price or charge.

clue.text: Relearn on regular basis after court equipment fraud

indicators.note: regular means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: a racket is used on a tennis or squash court
the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A player must relearn their game after a sports equipment scam.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'after' means the letters from Relearn come after the court gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A racketeer runs a dishonest business, and fraud can mean a person who swindles or deceives others.

clue.text: Cock-up initially, guarantee harsh criticism

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of cock-up
to ensure is to make certain, guarantee

explanation.surface: A blunder is certain to draw fierce condemnation.
explanation.walkthrough: A cock-up is British slang for a botched job.
explanation.definitionFit: Censure is formal strong disapproval or rebuke, the expression of severe blame.

clue.text: Controversial ground on net?

blocks.note: the e- prefix, as in e-mail, means electronic or online
a ground for doing something is a reason or motive

explanation.surface: A disputed patch of turf, or an argument raging on the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On net' comes after 'ground' in the clue, but its letter goes first: 'on' puts it on top.
explanation.definitionFit: An emotive issue arouses strong feeling, which makes it contentious and likely to cause heated argument.

clue.text: British articles for swim

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for British
the two English articles, indefinite and definite

explanation.surface: Items of British swimwear on sale.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage to bathe means taking a dip in the sea or a river, going for a recreational paddle.

clue.text: Extremely bitter one’s let off, show anger

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only the outer letters are kept
off means gone wrong or spoiled, so the letters fall out of order

blocks.note: the first and last letters
one is I, and the apostrophe s is 'is'
these three letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone very bitter after being let off reacts angrily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let off' reads as a pardon, but 'off' is the anagram signal working on 'let'.
explanation.definitionFit: To bristle is to react with indignation, like an animal raising its hackles when provoked.

clue.text: Manoeuvres using diplomacy in circumstances sensitive at the outset

indicators.note: the outset is the beginning, so each of the three words gives its opening letter

blocks.note: tact is skill in handling people delicately
the first letters of these three words

explanation.surface: Delicate negotiations are conducted with tact when the situation is touchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At the outset' covers all three words before it, not only the last.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactics are the planned moves and methods used to achieve an aim, especially in battle or games.

clue.text: Greeting recalled VIP, judge, for us

indicators.note: recalled can mean called back, so the next word is read backwards

blocks.note: a nob is a toff or bigwig
J is the abbreviation for judge
our means belonging to us

explanation.surface: A dignitary and a judge are called back to deal with something on our behalf.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonjour is the French for good day, a standard salutation used when meeting someone.

clue.text: Genuine claim

blocks.note: first meaning: real, proper
second meaning: an entitlement

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means real or correct; as a noun it means an entitlement someone may assert.

clue.text: Shock treatment — percentage of asset value deducted

blocks.note: first meaning: what a barber does to a shock, a thick mass of hair
second meaning: the finance term for a reduction in an asset's valuation

explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock treatment' suggests electrotherapy, but a shock here is a mop of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A trim tidies a head of hair, and in banking the same word names the discount applied to collateral.

clue.text: Evading notice by deceiving? Not at first

indicators.note: not at first means the opening letter is taken away

blocks.note: deluding someone is deceiving them

explanation.surface: Someone escapes detection by trickery.
explanation.definitionFit: To elude is to escape or avoid being caught or seen, so the participle means slipping past attention.

clue.text: Retains redeveloped drink

indicators.note: redeveloped means rebuilt in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: these seven letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A redeveloped bar keeps serving the same drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin, an alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Still raven, ever the lesser-spotted, hides

indicators.note: the phrase before it hides something inside its run of letters

blocks.note: running across the word boundaries, from the last letter of the bird
surface padding completing the bird-name picture

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher's note that the raven, and the rarer spotted variety, stays out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'lesser-spotted' bit mimics a bird name, like the lesser spotted woodpecker.
explanation.definitionFit: Still and the answer are both adverbs meaning in spite of that, used to concede a point.
